Their first computer

Asus is donating 100 desktop PCs to an NGO. Many of the people who will use them have never touched a computer, and power and internet come and go. Which free operating system should they run?

What an operating system is

On its own, a computer is just metal and plastic. The operating system is the software that wakes it up: the desktop, the windows, the files and every app you open.

Windows and macOS are the famous ones — they cost money and keep their code secret. Our three finalists do the same job, for free.

Why free and open

Free means no licence fee to pay — on one computer or on all one hundred. Open means anyone can see how it works, run it, copy it and share it.

€0to put the same system on every PC

No software bill as the lab grows, and updates a teacher can carry from one PC to the next on a USB stick.

Who we’re choosing for

100identical PCs for years of use
1stcomputer for many users; no Windows habits
Lowpower and internet: unreliable or missing

Our priority: easy to use, even without internet.

About 100 in, 3 out

About 100 systems, mostly Linux. Four questions:

  1. Is it free and open?Out: ChromeOS Flex — free, but closed.
  2. Is it still updated?Out: abandoned projects with no security updates.
  3. Can a beginner use it?Out: Arch, Gentoo, FreeBSD — for experts.
  4. Best of its kind?Out: Ubuntu, Lubuntu, Puppy — stronger finalists.

How they score

Ratings from sources and reviews: 1–5. Adjust the weights.

With equal weights: Endless OS 20, Linux Mint 18, Zorin OS Lite 16, out of 25.

Our pick

Endless OS

  • Works offline. Encyclopedia, lessons and apps included.
  • Hard to break. All-or-nothing updates; previous version kept.
  • Made for beginners. A familiar phone-like home screen.

Plan B Linux Mint for reliable internet and office skills.

1Prepare the USB

Download Endless OS Full.
Create a reformatter USB (32 GB or more).

2Install on 100 PCs

Boot from USB, install, then repeat.
10 sticks × 10 rounds = 100 PCs.

After the install

  1. Train local helpersTeach 5–10 people; they help the rest.
  2. Update by USBDownload once, share with every PC.

Fun fact

The IBM system

The heaviest system to run

This operating system runs on IBM’s Z mainframes, built for big business. IBM charges for it every month.

Questions?

Our pick is Endless OS, because a computer should keep working when the internet doesn’t. Plan B is Linux Mint.
